column1: # Proto-Min GOLD set — reconstructions transcribed from a published authority
# (Jerry Norman's Proto-Min reconstruction: Norman 1973 "Tonal development in
# Min", 1974 "The initials of Proto-Min", and his later finals / strata work,
# refined w/ W. South Coblin). Consumed by `python -m hanzihub.eval_protomin`
# to measure the rule-based reconstructor (reconstruct.py) against this gold.
#   1. Every `proto_min` value MUST come from a real published source. NEVER
#      invent or guess a form: a fabricated gold form yields a confident, FALSE
#      accuracy number and is strictly worse than an empty file.
#   3. Notation: IPA segments; a leading reconstruction `*` is optional (the
#      scorer strips it); tone as a trailing digit (1-8) or superscript. The
#      scorer segments each form into (onset, rhyme, tone) for per-slot scoring,
#      so keep the segmental order onset+rhyme+tone.
#   4. One Han character per row. Columns are TAB-separated.
# The first non-comment line below is the header. Add gold rows beneath it.
# Forms below are Norman's full reconstructions (onset + rhyme + tone-category
# A/B/C/D = 平/上/去/入) as recorded in the English Wiktionary/Wikipedia "Proto-Min"
# article, which cites Norman with page numbers. Stored VERBATIM in Norman's
# notation (tš/dž/š, tone letters, ɑ, softened *-/*h series); the scorer bridges
# that notation to the reconstructor's IPA before comparing. The `citation` keeps
# Norman's ref AND flags the immediate source (Wikipedia) for later verification
